## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Its opening canonical verse begins with the phrase *kiccassa kattāraṃ* [Fausböll 1877; Anandajoti 2010].

According to the narrative frame preserved in the commentary, the Buddha related the story while residing at Jetavana with reference to his prominent lay benefactor Anāthapiṇḍika. In the concluding identification of the birth story (*samodhāna*), the Buddha explains the rebirth connections: the ungrateful border merchant (*paccantavāsī*) of the past corresponds to the same borderer in the present, whereas the merchant of Bārāṇasī (*Bārāṇasīseṭṭhī*) was the Bodhisatta himself [Fausböll 1877].
